environment.pinned: Docling 2.129.0, docling-core 2.96.0, content-core 2.0.7, pandas 3.0.0, RapidOCR 3.9.2, SurrealDB SDK 1.0.8

findings.summary: Native PDF from a URL can no longer run after a patch refusal.
Conversion verdict is checked before serialization on both paths; vectors are generated first and replaced in one revision-fenced transaction.
evidence: 128 D10/D11 tests passed on standalone SurrealDB 2.3.10 (RocksDB)
residual: embedded-engine evidence does not cover concurrency
native non-PDF image scans are not verdict-checked (baseline behaviour)

findings.summary: A hyphen closes only on same-margin line-break evidence; ambiguous geometry keeps the separator and every hyphen.
residual: extra space for identifiers wrapped in centred headings or after an indented first line (safe direction)

findings.summary: Attached notes pass through the active text serializer; literal # and > are escaped in Legal, written once.
Release mode compares bytes and validates both manifest inventories.
residual: diagnostic (non --release) mode still normalizes and can return 0 for an unlabelled export

findings.summary: Model identity and free-standing orientation evidence are closed. Candidate span text is still not bound to the TSV rows it cites.
Each hyphenated OCR row needs its own ordered, single-use output span; no aggregate count is used.
residual: non-hyphen rows and elements are reusable; evidence is unsigned

findings.summary: Prepared hashes are kept until a verified pair exists; no fresh checksum is ever blessed.
residual: archive visible without .sha256 until the next build after a persistent write error
old hash restored beside the new archive when interrupted right after the rename

findings.summary: Eight business tables are content-hashed; F0 8/8 and N0 pass on the embedded engine and on the standalone server.
residual: 14 of 22 tables are outside the fingerprint and have no preservation method in the repository

new_findings.scope: release acceptance gate only (scripts/ocr/phase12_standard_diff.py); no runtime code
new_findings.code_path: verify_bound_output: baseline text is rebuilt from TSV rows, candidate text is taken from the candidate's own element record; cell text and the joined span are never compared with the rows; the cell walk breaks instead of refusing
new_findings.reproduction: candidate text join changes or drops a token inside an OCR text span whose baseline still rebuilds from its rows
new_findings.consequence: exit 0, class 'expected TSV fix', G-H1 'verified' for 'Điều 5' -> 'Điều 6' and a dropped 'không' that the candidate's own TSV rows contradict
new_findings.minimal_fix: accept a changed span only when every bound cell text equals its TSV row, the walk consumes the whole span, each difference is a row whose upstream form differs or a hyphen closure, and attached notes point at a recorded source element; otherwise NOT VERIFIED

new_findings.relation: side effect of the D10-02 embedding fence
new_findings.summary: Any write to the Source record between the embed job's load and commit ends the job as a non-retried 'Source changed before publication'; unchanged text is left without vectors until a manual re-embed.
new_findings.minimal_fix: stop permanently only when the Source is deleted or its text changed; a revision-only miss must be retryable

new_findings.relation: side effect of the D10-04 fix; Legal mode only (default off)
new_findings.summary: Every Legal footnote is now backslash-escaped for _ [ ] * ~ ` and clause markers, unlike the same body text and unlike 2cc824f (F-17: stored text is the printed text).
new_findings.minimal_fix: footnotes pass through escape_literal_block_syntax only, like body paragraphs

known_limitations: image scans through content-core's native path are not verdict-checked
the two upstream patch groups are not installed as one transaction (fail-closed)
stderr PIPE capture can exceed the 4096-byte classification limit
the release diff gate returns NOT VERIFIED for hyphenated tokens in headings, list items, footers, tables and cross-page merges; exit 0 on real legal PDFs is unlikely
diff evidence carries hashes, not signatures
